summary: Fact-check katz/CLAUDE_REPORT.md numbers and claims against result files, git history and the brief

errors.problem: The Kalshi d30 Brier is rounded wrong. The source value is 0.094457, which rounds to 0.094. The 0.095 comes from rounding the log's printed 0.0945 a second time. n, best model, K10 and base rate in this row are all correct.

errors.sentence: | 7 days before decision | 36 | **0.081** | 0.192 (K10s) | 0.193 (reproduces Amendment 2) | 0.203 |
errors.problem: The Kalshi d7 Brier is rounded wrong. The source value is 0.080480, which rounds to 0.080. The 0.081 comes from rounding the printed 0.0805 a second time. The other cells are correct, and K10's 0.1929 does reproduce Amendment 2.

errors.sentence: An independent recomputation matched every number to 1e-16 and a bug hunt found no error
errors.problem: This overstates the verification. The recompute says sharpness_sd did NOT match: it was off by 2.0e-5 to 3.2e-5, a ddof convention difference that matches when recomputed with ddof = 1. The DSRs were only checked for internal consistency: they all imply the same SR0 = 0.4678. The verifier says it 'could not rebuild the pool's variance itself', so the DSR values were never independently reproduced. CPCV path and split std/worst are not in the list of recomputed columns either.
errors.correct: An independent recompute matched the Brier, accuracy, sign-test, McNemar, Holm, CPCV-mean, PBO and SR columns to about 1e-16. sharpness_sd differed only by the ddof convention. The DSRs were checked for internal consistency only (common SR0), not rebuilt. The bug hunt found no error.
errors.source: scotus-predict-v2/katz/results/claude/selection_verification_2026-10-13.json (recompute findings: 'Only sharpness_sd differed...'; 'I could not rebuild the pool's variance itself')

errors.sentence: The big misses are the affirmances the model never sees coming (Skrmetti, Moore, the marijuana-gun case, GVG, NPPC, tariffs), where Kalshi had moved to 0.07-0.27.
errors.problem: GVG (Gonzalez v. Google) was not an affirmance. SCDB codes it as vacated and remanded (caseDisposition 5, partyWinning 0). The other five are affirmances (caseDisposition 2). The d7 Kalshi range of 0.07-0.265 is correct.
errors.correct: Skrmetti, Moore, Hemani (marijuana-gun), NPPC and V.O.S. Selections (tariffs) were affirmed. Gonzalez v. Google was vacated and remanded, and petitioner still lost.

errors.sentence: The only notable improvement anywhere in the project so far is the box agent's oral-argument trial K16 (0.1979 vs K10 0.2052 on 1990-2014), which did not pass its own significance gate
errors.problem: K17 (K16 plus sentiment) improved almost exactly as much, 0.1984 vs 0.2052, and came closer to significance (sign-test p_holm 0.059 vs K16's 0.130; DSR 0.957 vs 0.967 at N = 26). Calling K16 'the only' notable improvement leaves K17 out.
errors.correct: K16 0.1979 (p_holm 0.130, DSR_N26 0.967) and K17 0.1984 (p_holm 0.059, DSR_N26 0.957) vs K10 0.2052, all-cases/reverse metric, 1990-2014. Neither passed the Holm gate.

errors.sentence: K16 (question counts) is the one trial that moved Brier materially (0.1979), but it is not significant after Holm (p 0.13), its DSR (0.97 at N = 26) would be lower at N = 37
errors.problem: Same problem as above: K17 also moved Brier materially (0.1984). The quoted K16 numbers (0.1979, p_holm 0.13, DSR 0.97 at N = 26) are correct.
errors.correct: K16 0.1979 and K17 0.1984 both moved Brier materially. K17's p_holm is 0.059 and its DSR_N26 is 0.957.

errors.problem: K10 as recorded has no CPCV score: its CPCV columns are empty, and the report's own table shows '-'. On CPCV the KC trials can only be compared with K10s.
errors.correct: Every new trial is worse than K10 on the selection window (WF 0.2272-0.2277 vs 0.2231) and on the holdout (0.2215-0.2221 vs 0.2119). On CPCV they are worse than K10s (0.2259-0.2265 vs 0.2199). K10 itself has no CPCV value.

missing: Brief gate missing: Holm McNemar vs always-reverse/always-petitioner results are never given, even though the brief lists this gate. From selection_1990_2014.csv, WF: KC1 55/53 (p_holm 1.0), KC2 42/50 (1.0), KC3 111/107 (1.0), KC4 109/111 (1.0); K10 96/55 (p_holm 0.0064); K10s 133/99 (0.150). CPCV vs AR: all KC p_holm 1.0. Always-petitioner accuracy is 1,436/2,250 = 63.8%, so KC2 (63.5%) and KC4 (63.7%) are below the trivial rule and KC1 (63.9%) and KC3 (64.0%) are level with it. On the holdout, KC1's accuracy (0.6697) equals the always-petitioner rate (517/772).

Brief gate missing: the report links the calibration plot but never says what it shows. WF ECE: K10 as recorded 0.061 (overconfident; mean P 0.69 vs a 0.638 base rate), K10s 0.024, KC1-KC4 0.025-0.034. CPCV ECE is 0.020-0.027. The holdout calibration plot (results/claude/HOLDOUT_calibration_claude.png), which C1 registered, is not mentioned.

PBO caveat incomplete: the report calls PBO 0.0 vacuous but omits the verification's challenger-only diagnostic PBO of 0.40 (WF) and 0.586 (CPCV). The CPCV value is above the 0.5 threshold. Source: selection_verification_2026-10-13.json.

Box agent's Amendment 6 results (K24 0.1972, K25 0.1983; PBO 0.186; DSR_N32 0.926/0.941; Holm p 0.146; K10 stays) are missing. They finished at 20:35 PT, before the report, and change the 'only notable improvement' claim and next step 1. Source: katz-a6/STATUS_K24.md, eval_k2425/.

Disagreement tracker: the registered hypothetical paper P&L is left out. At d30 it is K10 +0.54 and KC1 -0.88; at d7 it is K10 +0.26 and KC1 -0.58. K10's flagged-market P&L is positive at both times, which matters for the Kalshi-edge question even though it is small-n and was never traded. Source: HOLDOUT_DISAGREE_summary_claude.csv.
No explicit statement that K10 stays the forward model (verdict.json: replaces_K10 = false, used_for_forward = K10). The forward section discusses KC1 instead.

Kalshi argument-morning context: at the arg time (n = 18), no model beats the prior-10-term base rate (0.2048). The best model, KC2, scores 0.2055, and K10 scores 0.2217. Source: HOLDOUT_kalshi_settled_claude.csv.
K10s's DSR_cpcv of 0.955 (just above the 0.95 gate) appears in the table with no explanation. Its WF DSR is 0.84, and it is a non-selectable comparator, as the verification notes.

Holdout-exposure caveat leaves out C1's own pre-registration peek. The C1 honesty log says the label-availability counts printed the 2015-2025 0/1 split (517 petitioner wins of 772) before registration. Source: AMENDMENT_C1_CLAUDE.md lines 22-23.
